According to the troubleshooting guide for when the engine does not start, perform the following checks [p. 119]:

- **Ignition / Engine kill switch:** If the ignition/Engine kill switch is in the OFF position, switch ON ignition [p. 119].
- **Fuel level:** If there is an inadequate fuel level in the fuel tank, top up the fuel [p. 119].
- **Battery / charging circuit:** If the lights are dim or the horn sound is weak, this indicates a weak or discharged battery / problem in charging circuit; contact an Authorised service center [p. 119].
- **Fuses:** If a fuse is blown, replace the fuse with the same rating; contact an Authorised service center if the problem persists [p. 119].
- **Spark plug connections:** If there is a connection issue with the spark plug, cap, or high tension cable, reconnect the spark plug, cap, and high tension cable [p. 119].

If the problem is not rectified after these checks, get the motorcycle checked by a Royal Enfield Authorised Dealer / Service Centre [p. 119].

### Additional starting instructions
- **Starter operation:** Push and hold the electric start switch for a maximum of 5 seconds [p. 71]. If the engine does not start within 5 seconds, release the starter switch and wait for about 5 seconds before attempting to start again [p. 72].
- **Multiple attempts:** In case the vehicle is not starting on multiple continuous attempts, turn OFF and turn ON the ignition switch and then start again [p. 72].
- **Side stand:** Ensure the side stand is retracted before moving / starting; the vehicle may start with the side stand down, but the engine will turn off when a gear is engaged due to the side stand cut-off feature [p. 72].

**CAUTION:**
> "If the engine does not start. Do not hold the starter switch in depressed condition for long periods, this will cause the battery to drain below the threshold level of 10 V. Please get the motorcycle checked through an Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre to identify and correct the reason for not starting." [p. 72]

**From the manual**

Under the Troubleshooting section for the symptom of **"Poor pickup"** when the **"engine RPM raises disproportionately to the vehicle speed"**, the manual specifies the following remedy:
- Adjust the clutch free play and contact an Authorised service center [p. 120].

### Clutch Cable Free Play Inspection / Adjustment Procedure
The manual provides the following steps to inspect and adjust the clutch cable free play:
1. Ensure the cable is fitted correctly [p. 99].
2. Turn the steering handlebar to the right-hand lock position [p. 99].
3. Using a 12 mm spanner, loosen the adjusting nut closest to the lifter arm fully [p. 99].
4. Adjust the position of the inner adjusting nut to provide 9–11 mm of free play at the clutch lever ball end (from its furthest position) before engine engagement [p. 99].
5. Pull the lever 3 times and check the gap again; adjust as per the previous steps if necessary [p. 100].
6. Using both spanners, tighten the nut closest to the lifter arm without moving the inner nut [p. 100].
7. Rotate the handlebar 5 or more times, return it to a straight position, and re-check the free play in the lever [p. 100].
8. Adjust as per steps 3 and 4 if necessary [p. 100].

### CAUTION
The manual states:
- "If you are not comfortable to adjust free play as per stated procedure, please visit near by service centre." [p. 100]
- "If desired free play is not achieved or there is a suspect of clutch slip- keep positive free play & reach nearest service centre." [p. 100]
- "Adjuster nut should rest properly in the threaded region." [p. 100]
- "Clutch free play should be checked and adjusted only when the engine is cold." [p. 100]
- "During clutch play checking, check the clutch cable for any abnormality as it is in vehicle condition." [p. 100]
- "If any abnormality suspected, reach nearest service centre." [p. 100]

**From the manual**

### Starting Procedure
1. **Ensure side stand is retracted**: The vehicle may start with the side stand down, but the engine will turn off when a gear is engaged; ensure the side stand is retracted before moving or starting the vehicle [p. 72].
2. **Shift into neutral**: Move the motorcycle back and forth gently while simultaneously shifting the gear [p. 70, p. 73]. Ensure the gear is in the neutral position and the neutral lamp is glowing on the instrument cluster [p. 70, p. 73].
   - "CAUTION: Do not attempt to shift gears without moving the motorcycle back and forth as it will damage the gears mechanism." [p. 73]
3. **Turn switches ON**: Turn the ignition key to the ON position and the engine kill switch on the right-hand side handlebar to the run position [p. 70].
4. **Check instruments**: Check the fuel level indicator; if the last bar is blinking continuously, refuel immediately [p. 71]. After the vehicle is started, the Malfunction Indicator Lamp (MIL) will glow for a few seconds and turn OFF [p. 70].
   - "CAUTION: In case the malfunction indicator does not turn OFF, get the motorcycle checked through an Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre for rectification." [p. 71]
5. **Disengage clutch**: Pull in and hold the clutch lever in the depressed condition [p. 71, p. 73].
6. **Press starter button**: Push and hold the electric start switch/starter button until the engine starts, for a maximum of 5 seconds [p. 71]. Do not release the button before the engine starts [p. 73].
   - If the engine does not start within 5 seconds, release the starter switch and wait about 5 seconds before attempting again [p. 72]. 
   - After three successive crankings, do not press the starter button for more than 5 seconds, and wait 15 to 20 seconds for the battery to recover [p. 73].
   - If the vehicle does not start on multiple continuous attempts, turn the ignition switch OFF and ON, then try starting again [p. 72].
   - "CAUTION: If the engine does not start. Do not hold the starter switch in depressed condition for long periods, this will cause the battery to drain below the threshold level of 10 V. Please get the motorcycle checked through an Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre to identify and correct the reason for not starting." [p. 72]

---

### Cold Idle / Warm-up Time
- Never accelerate as soon as the engine starts, especially in cold conditions [p. 73].
- The engine must be allowed to idle for **at least 120 seconds** to allow engine oil to circulate, lubricate all internal moving parts, and raise the engine temperature [p. 73]. Failure to follow this will cause serious damage to internal engine components [p. 73].
- Accelerate only after the idling RPM has stabilized and is consistent [p. 73].

**From the manual**

### What is wrong
* An increase in engine speed during acceleration and constant speed running without an increase in vehicle speed indicates **clutch slip** [p. 81].
* Clutch slip causes high fuel consumption, poor acceleration, and overheating of the engine [p. 81].

---

### What you should do

1. **Check and adjust clutch lever free play:**
   * The free play of the clutch lever should be 8 to 13 mm as measured at the clutch lever end at the handlebar before the clutch begins to disengage [p. 93].
   * Ensure that the engine is cold (engine oil at room temperature) [p. 93].
   * Adjust the free play at the clutch release arm if it is found to be more [p. 93]:
     1. Ensure the engine is cold [p. 93].
     2. Loosen the lock nut while holding the clutch cable adjusting nut [p. 93].
     3. Adjust the clutch cable adjusting nut "in" or "out" to give sufficient play in the clutch lever [p. 93].
     4. After adjusting the play, hold the adjuster nut in the same position and tighten the lock nut [p. 93].

2. **If the problem persists:**
   * If the condition persists even after adjusting the clutch lever play, immediately have the clutch checked by a TVS Motor Company Authorised Main Dealer / Authorised Dealer [p. 81].

---

### Warnings and Cautions from the manual

"Caution
Never drive the vehicle with the clutch lever pressed. This will reduce the life of clutch and affect the vehicle performance and fuel economy." [p. 81]

"Caution
Too much or too less clutch lever free play will damage the clutch plates, thereby affecting the performance of the vehicle. Adjust the clutch lever free play only when the engine is cold. After adjusting free play properly, if there is a clutch slip or there is difficulty in shifting gear, visit your TVS Motor Company Authorised Main Dealer / Authorised Dealer for rectification." [p. 93]

To start the engine of your TVS Ronin:

1. Turn the ignition switch to the 'ON' position [p. 78]. The instrument cluster and warning lights will go through a self-diagnostic cycle; make sure all warning lights on the cluster come on during this phase [p. 78].
2. Verify the following conditions before starting the engine [p. 78]:
   - The engine cut-off switch is turned 'ON' [p. 26] (in the run position [p. 78]).
   - The side stand is retracted [p. 78].
   - The transmission is in neutral [p. 78].
   - If gears are engaged, the clutch lever must be engaged/pressed completely [p. 26, p. 78].
3. Press the electric starter switch without applying the throttle [p. 78]. 
4. Release the starter switch immediately/as soon as the engine starts [p. 26, p. 78]. The engine will not start or crank if the throttle is opened more than 30% [p. 78].

**Cautions:**
- "Do not keep the engine in idling rpm for long. Do not open excessive throttle when the vehicle is parked. It leads to overheating of engine and damage to the internal components." [p. 78]
- "Operation of electric start switch with clutch lever not in completely pressed position can lead to jerking of the vehicle, to prevent such unexpected behavior it is recommended to press the clutch lever completely." [p. 26]

**From the manual**

### Petrol Specification & Octane Rating
* Use only BS VI petrol with a minimum octane rating of **RON 98** [p. 80], [p. 125].

### Ethanol-Blended Petrol
* BS VI petrol containing **up to 20% ethanol by volume** (E20) can be used [p. 80], [p. 125].

**Additional fuel guidance from the manual:**
* Using petrol with higher than 20% ethanol content can:
  * Degrade plastic and rubber components of the fuel system and vehicle parts [p. 80].
  * Cause corrosion damage to metal parts such as the fuel tank [p. 80].
  * Result in startability and drivability issues [p. 80].
  * Decrease fuel economy [p. 80].
* The manufacturer states it is "not responsible for any warranty issues that results from using ethanol blend in excess of 20% by volume" [p. 80].
* Ethanol absorbs water very easily, leading to fuel separation. Take extra care to prevent moisture entry into the fuel tank when refuelling or washing the vehicle [p. 80].
* Painted parts (such as panels and covers) must not come into contact with ethanol-blended fuels [p. 80].
* "In case of any abnormalities observed due to use of ethanol blended fuels, customers are advised to use a different fuel station/brand for standard E20 fuel or contact authorised service centres" [p. 80].
* Never mix oil and petrol in the fuel tank, and always fill fuel from reputed and reliable fuel stations [p. 80].

### Meaning of 'HIGH ENGINE TEMP'
* The cluster displays **HIGH ENGINE TEMP** "If the engine temperature is greater than threshold value" [p. 61].

### Coolant Top-Up
* The manual does not describe coolant or a procedure for topping up coolant.
* Under the **COOLING SYSTEM** section, the manual states: 
  > "TVS RONIN is designed with an external oil cooler arrangement for optimal engine cooling. The oil cooler is mounted in front of the engine which improves the engine durability and provides better heat management without compromising the engine performance." [p. 67]

* **Clutch slip:** "The clutch slip will cause high fuel consumption, poor acceleration and overheating of engine. If the condition persists even after adjusting the clutch lever play, immediately have the clutch checked by TVS Motor Company Authorised Main Dealer / Authorised Dealer." [p. 81]

* **Engine oil:** "Dirty or less engine cum transmission oil increases the friction between various parts of the engine and reduces the engine life, thereby increases fuel consumption. Regularly inspect the engine cum transmission oil for correct level and top-up if necessary." [p. 81]
